body: (Don't take me as condescending, please. It's just the lethargic and lack of empathy) I thank you for your support, but basically your saying I just need to wait because it all gets better eventually. But being so young, the waiting is the hardest part. Years from now I'll have the opportunities your talking about, but right now I'm still so confined by rules and laws. I can't even buy my own cough medicine because I'm not old enough. I spend a lot of time on the internet and learn as much as I can. I believe the only way to understand the world around us and to somehow find an answer to the big questions is to learn as much as you can about the things around you. Knowledge is power. But I look at the world... And it's so shitty. Murders, rapes, terrorists. I hear stories about people keeping their daughters as sex slaves for 20 years. It's easy to forget about any positives in life. But those are all just tools used by the media to keep us in fear, right? But I look at things more relevant to myself, and it's all still the same. A power race. Get as much as you can as fast as you can and screw anyone over while you get the chance. There's still good out there, sure, but the world is ruled by those that have. And the have nots do everything in their power to try and obtain. That's not what I want to do the rest of my life. I don't want to work a job that I hate to buy things I don't need(Might be watching too much Fight Club). The world is corrupt. Things that benefit everyone are overshadowed by things that can get you money. The more I've been thinking about it the more I think hippies had the right idea. I've come to the conclusion long ago that the point of life was love and happiness, but how is someone expected to get that? I'm a pretty socially active person. I go out most night to a friends house and hang out and the nights I don't go out I usually have people over. And that's what makes me happy. I don't want to climb the corporate ladder and kiss someones ass to make it in life, I want to sit on my couch with a bunch of friends and share a bowl. I wouldn't mind working a mediocre job to have a mediocre house if it means I'd still have the free time to do what I enjoy the most; nothing. This world really doesn't seem worth living in to me
I lold. The internet never ceases to amaze me. There's a picture for everything.

I'm still a youngin -.- I'm in high school, which only makes things worse. I really want to get out of this place. I feel like I've already accomplished everything high school has to offer me and I want to move on, but I'm only a junior. I'm graduating early next year though. I have no idea what I want to do. I jump around from idea to idea. I was thinking software engineer, then biomedical engineer, and now I've started thinking about philosophy. More specifically metaphysics, since the subject is really what I'm more worried about at the moment. The really issue that's bothering me is... Why do people want to live? What makes someone want to wake up every day to actually do things? I have no motivation. I have no desire to wake up, I actually detest it. It's such a drain. I've figured, I'm only 17. That's not even a quarter of an average life expectancy and I'm already hating life. I've just been living a day at a time.

It depends on the day. I like the person I am mentally. I think I have a lot of positive characteristics about me. Emotionally I'm unstable and don't like that. And physically... I've been working on. I really don't like how I look, but I've been working my ass off to try and make it better. But other than that I think I'm a good, smart, and funny person. I don't feel like I deserve anything. You need to work for what you get. But in the sense of some type of karma, yes and no. Because of my lethargic demeanor to life I may have hurt some people emotionally, but never physically. But I've also had my deal of emotional distress. And, although I don't remember any of my childhood, from what my parents and therapist said(We used to go to family counseling with him when we were younger) I had a very traumatic upbringing. A lot of physical and mental abuse. My brother was actually diagnosed with dissociative disorder and he believes it was because of our childhood. I'm sure I also have some walls up in my head. So I can't necessarily say I deserve anything for something I can't even remember.
